column60: Zhang et al. (2026, *Tectonics*) develop new U-Pb petrochronology and thermochronology datasets from zircon, garnet, titanite, rutile, and apatite from the Adirondack Highlands. Probabilistic thermal history inversion of these data shows that the Adirondack Highlands cooled slowly throughout the Tonian, with the magnetite-carried remanence in the Marcy Massif anorthosite acquired ca. **887 ± 23 Ma** — about 85 Myr later than the ca. 970 Ma cooling-curve estimate of Brown and McEnroe (2012). Zhang et al. additionally report a positive inverse baked-contact test in which an unmetamorphosed mafic dike (site GD1) bakes its anorthosite host (site MA11); because such dikes intrude Proterozoic but not Paleozoic rocks in the region (Fisher, 1977) and are correlated with Ediacaran dikes dated elsewhere in the Grenville Province (Kamo et al., 1995; Halls et al., 2015), the test demonstrates that the anorthosite magnetite remanence is Proterozoic in age. This revised age fills a critical gap in the Laurentia apparent polar wander path between the ca. 990 Ma Jacobsville Formation pole and the ca. 780 Ma Gunbarrel pole, with implications for the position of Rodinia in the early to mid-Tonian.

Van Schmus et al., 1993), the age adopted by Meert & Stuckey (2002). A

acidic rocks carrying the paleomagnetic remanence belong to the older
1.48-1.45 Ga episode. Taking the spread of in-situ dates from that episode gives
a nominal age of 1466 Ma with bounds of 1448-1484 Ma, adopted here in place of
the older 1476 ± 16 Ma value.
